analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of docs/developer/test.md (lines 1–945) and the bounded change map/patch. Changes are a date update and an Add-On Hold testing section at HEAD 767–790; the latter's patch is truncated. No supported security regression follows from these documentation changes alone. Existing guidance preserves isolated state, encrypted-cache qualification and tenant refusal (BASE 577–619), stop-before-revocation tests (749–766), and separate Apple/runtime authorization gates (787–880).
The new section describes a local AF_UNIX/flock control surface, owner-only records, peer checks, bounded drain, lease expiry/restart restoration, and busy fields carried through heartbeat and registration. These implicate TB-003/TB-002, availability (T-010/T-029), and authorization continuity (T-053); test descriptions do not establish implementation controls or execution results. Integration should examine the actual add-on IPC peer authentication, socket/record/path permissions and stale-socket handling, lease/lock recovery, drain ownership, and cross-file reconnect/update/stop behavior against the provider serving and authorization gates. Confirm busy-wire handling does not substitute for final authorization or reopen held admission. This batch supplies no implementation or complete HEAD section, so these contracts remain unverified rather than findings. T-041's cache isolation, encryption and staging requirements remain relevant if hold/unload changes native retirement or cache ownership.
